subsection.title: Finding the Volume of a Solid of Revolution
subsection.paragraph: In this section we use a Riemann sum to find a formula for computing the volume of a solid that results when a region is revolved about an axis. The solid is called a solid of revolution . To find the volume of a solid of revolution, suppose the plane region under the curve defined by a nonnegative continuous function $$y = f(x)$$ between $$x = a$$ and $$x = b$$ is revolved about the $$x$$ -axis (Figure 16).

The solid has been obtained by shading the region the curve in graph a has swept as it was rotated about the x axis.

subsection.paragraph: To derive a formula for finding the volume of the solid of revolution, we divide the interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ into $$n$$ subintervals, each of equal length, by means of the points $$x_{0} = a,x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{n} = b$$ , so that the length of each subinterval is given by $$\Delta x = {\left( {b - a} \right) \slash n}$$ . Also, let $$p_{1},p_{2},\ldots,p_{n}$$ be points in the subintervals $$\left\lbrack {x_{0},x_{1}} \right\rbrack,\left\lbrack {x_{1},x_{2}} \right\rbrack,\ldots,\left\lbrack {x_{n - 1},x_{n}} \right\rbrack$$ , respectively (Figure 17).

subsection.paragraph: Let’s concentrate on the part of the solid of revolution that is swept out by revolving the region under the curve between $$x = x_{i - 1}$$ and $$x = x_{i}$$ about the $$x$$ -axis.
